intro.data: A process turns one thing into another. Two machines both accept the messy spreadsheet — but they do different things to it. Before you run, predict what each would produce, then build the one that makes a clean table.
intro.alchemy: A process turns one material into another. Two apparatuses both accept the raw ore — but they do different things to it. Predict what each would produce, then build the one that makes a pure ingot.
intro.spellcraft: A working turns one essence into another. Two runes both accept the wild spark — but they do different things to it. Predict what each would produce, then build the one that makes a steady flame.
intro.abstract: A morphism turns one object into another. Two machines both accept the input value but produce different outputs. Build the one that yields the goal.

goal.data: Wire the input through a machine so it comes out as the clean table.
goal.alchemy: Wire the input through an apparatus so it comes out as the pure ingot.
goal.spellcraft: Wire the input through a rune so it comes out as the steady flame.
goal.abstract: Wire the input through a machine so it produces the goal value.

afterSuccess.data: You watched the messy spreadsheet become a clean table. Both machines were the same type, but only one behaved the way you wanted — a process is defined by what it does, not just what it connects.
afterSuccess.alchemy: You watched the raw ore become a pure ingot. Both apparatuses were the same type, but only one behaved the way you wanted — a process is defined by what it does.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: You watched the wild spark become a steady flame. Both runes were the same type, but only one behaved the way you wanted — a working is defined by what it does.
afterSuccess.abstract: The input became the goal value. Same-typed morphisms can do different things; a morphism is defined by its behavior.

reveal.summary: The things being transformed are objects; the process between them is an arrow, or morphism. Two morphisms with the same source and target can still behave differently.
reveal.moreFormal: A morphism f: A → B has one source and one target. Knowing its type (A → B) is not the same as knowing what it does.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: f: (input: A) => B — two functions with the same signature can compute different things.
